what_it_does: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) refers to encryption schemes designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers; QC-MDPC McEliece is one such scheme, but it is slow and area-hungry when implemented on ordinary digital chips because it involves large matrix operations. This paper proposes using analog computing-in-memory (doing arithmetic directly inside the memory array using electrical signals, rather than shipping data to a separate processor) to accelerate those matrix multiplications. Analog circuits can perform many multiply-and-add operations simultaneously at low energy, though they introduce small numerical errors; the paper claims these errors remain within acceptable bounds for the cryptographic computation.
